$comment: THE ROLL ARCHIVE, which is where the storm stops being weather. Nine hundred years of rainfall records with a column of noughts in the summer rows and six numbers at the bottom that are not noughts is the single hardest piece of evidence in Act 5 that something is being done to Caelora rather than happening to it -- and the game never says so out loud, because a shelf saying it is better than a person saying it. The stranger reading the foreign shelf is the Averra note canon asks for: other regions, other leagues, other Kin.

lines: I have started your entry. Not the name - the name is the mason's. The paragraph is mine.
Come and correct it in about fifty years. Everybody's is wrong and nobody ever comes back.
Eight. Then you are a person this building is going to have to write about eventually.
Do not let that go to your head. So is everybody in the yard outside.
No desk, no counter, no gloves. They were written to be touched and they have been.
Second shelf on the left is the weather. I would start there, if I were you, this week.
I copy the damaged ones out before they go. Eleven volumes behind and always will be.
The 1712 flood took the middle of the fourth shelf. We are still guessing at forty names.
Nine hundred years of summers in this column and every one of them is a nought.
The last six lines are not noughts. I have read this page eleven times and it does not change.
It is not just here. The Skyreach wind logs go strange the same week. I checked.
My tutor says coincidence. My tutor has not looked at the Skyreach wind logs.
Six other leagues on this shelf and Caelora thinks it is the whole of Averra.
There is an island chain out east with a Kin that nests in the mast of a moving ship. Truly.
